name: Proxmox_VE_Cluster_Ceph
description: Ceph cluster health, OSD state, placement group state and capacity for a Proxmox VE hyper-converged cluster.
technicalNotes:
Single instance, one /cluster/ceph/status call per interval, whatever the size of the Ceph cluster. Requires Sys.Audit or Datastore.Audit on /. The Proxmox API declares this endpoint's return as an untyped object -- it passes through whatever `ceph status` produces -- so no field can be relied on from the schema, and Ceph has moved these keys between releases. Every field is therefore still read defensively, osdmap is accepted in both its flat and nested shapes, and each group of datapoints is withheld entirely when its source key is absent. That defensiveness is deliberate and should stay: one cluster's reply is not the schema.

Most Proxmox installs do not run Ceph. That case reports CephAvailable=0 and withholds everything else, rather than reporting a healthy cluster with zero OSDs. It is not a collection failure.

Health is three flags rather than one ordinal, because an encoding where 2 means HEALTH_ERR is something every dashboard author then has to look up. Placement group cleanliness is decided by decomposing the compound state name (active+clean, active+undersized+degraded) rather than by string-matching active+clean, so a state Ceph adds later does not silently count as clean.

Applies on the cluster role: resources whose pve.cluster.role is active or standby, which the NetScan sets. Only one of the pair collects -- the active resource, or the standby while the active one is down or has lost quorum. The other prints nothing, so its datapoints read No Data and the pair never alerts twice. The suite has no addCategory_* PropertySource: the NetScan sets the categories and pve.cluster.role, and the product page lists them for a resource added by hand.

Units: UsedBytes in bytes, as Ceph reports it. MB and GB are decimal (10^6 and 10^9 bytes); the product page states the suite's convention.

datapoints.name: CephAvailable
datapoints.description: 1 when Ceph status could be read. 0 on a cluster with no Ceph configured, in which case every other datapoint here is withheld.

datapoints.name: HealthWarn
datapoints.alertBody:
Ceph on the Proxmox cluster containing ##HOST## reports HEALTH_WARN. Data is still being served, but a condition needs attention before it becomes HEALTH_ERR; `ceph health detail` on any node names it.

Status: ##ALERTVALUEDISPLAYSTATUSNAME## (##VALUE##).

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: HealthError
datapoints.alertBody:
Ceph reports HEALTH_ERR. Data availability or durability is at risk; check `ceph health detail` on any node.

Status: ##ALERTVALUEDISPLAYSTATUSNAME## (##VALUE##).

datapoints.name: HealthChecks
datapoints.description: Number of active Ceph health checks. The checks are listed under Ceph in the Proxmox web interface, or by running ceph health detail on a node.

datapoints.name: OSDsDown
datapoints.alertBody:
##VALUE## Ceph OSD(s) on the Proxmox cluster containing ##HOST## are down. Their data is being served from the remaining replicas, so redundancy is reduced until they return. The Ceph OSD module shows which ones.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: OSDsOut
datapoints.description: OSDs known but not in the cluster. Expected during a planned rebalance.

datapoints.name: PGsClean
datapoints.description: Placement groups whose every state component is active or clean.

datapoints.name: PGsNotClean
datapoints.description: Placement groups in any other state: degraded, undersized, recovering, backfilling. Non-zero during normal recovery, so the threshold allows time to settle.
datapoints.alertBody:
##VALUE## Ceph placement group(s) on the Proxmox cluster containing ##HOST## are not active+clean (degraded, undersized, recovering or backfilling). This is normal briefly after an OSD restarts; if it persists, data has fewer copies than configured.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: UsedBytes
datapoints.description: Raw cluster capacity in use, bytes.

datapoints.name: UsedPercent
datapoints.description: Raw cluster utilisation. Ceph degrades badly when full, and rebalancing needs free space to work with.
datapoints.alertBody:
Ceph on the Proxmox cluster containing ##HOST## is ##VALUE##% full. Ceph slows and then blocks writes as it nears its full ratio, and recovering from an OSD failure needs free space to rebalance into.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: MonitorsInQuorum
datapoints.description: Ceph monitors currently in quorum. A cluster that loses monitor quorum is unavailable regardless of OSD state.
